newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures rise after consolidation.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures rise after consolidation.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were firmer in early dealings on Monday as the domestic debt market sought to advance after a consolidation period on Friday.
At 0720 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were up eight basis points at 101.93 points, while the 10-year benchmark cash Bund due July 2007 was at 102.53 with a yield of 5.65 percent.
"Maintain overall bullish profiles and use sell-offs as opportunities to buy further," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Futures & Options in a market commentary.
Traders also said the market has "safe-haven" support from the ongoing debate over the start of European monetary union.

Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber kept up his public crusade for a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty and its rules for membership in the currency union, saying he would call for a delay if entry criteria are weakened.

Stoiber, a top member of the conservative Christial Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), is threatening to block German membership in monetary union in the country's upper house of parliament.
Traders said the German debt market, which has recently been able to outperform the U.S. market despite losses in Treasuries, should keep on benefiting from EMU doubts.

The market also largely ignored Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer saying on Sunday that he hoped Germany could meet the Maastricht Treaty deficit goal this year but said sustainable budgetary discipline was more important than hitting targets.
Tietmeyer also indicated that he was comfortable with current low inflation levels and saw no reason to change monetary policies.
Traders said Tietmeyer's comments were nothing new.
"There was little over the weekend which could potentially shake Bunds out of their largely range-bound mood," MMS International said in a market commentary.

German market gains may also be limited ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Markets Committe meeting, at which no U.S. interest rate change is expected, and the issuance of Germany's 30-year Bund on Tuesday.

Some traders said the German market could seek to rally once the 30-year offering of up to 10 billion marks is completed, with some saying there was no correlation between the past when such offerings led to market tops.
"We do not believe current conditiosn correlate very well with the previous two precedents," DMG said of past cases of market tops at the time of 30-year debt issuances.
On a technical basis, traders said DTB September Bund futures face strong psychological resistance at 102.00 points, with further resistance evident at 102.14 and 102.30.
Support is evident at 101.75, 101.59 and 101.48 points.
